description:
We are SixersGoToSpace, a team of 4 and our roster is full.

We are a team of NTU Computer Science, Computer and Aerospace Engineering students taking on the Flame in Freefall challenge. Our strengths are in software, coding, and web development, plus hardware and design. We will use data analysis, data visualization, and statistics to pull insights out of the microgravity combustion data, and apply artificial intelligence and machine learning to build the fire safety models.
summary: Crew Health Monitor is a tablet-first web app that helps astronauts and their crew medical officer track health on long missions. It compares every astronaut with their own normal, not just Earth ranges, and links signals such as sleep, stress, temperature, heart rate and fluids into plain-language early warnings. It also includes space-specific self-checks, a hydration log and step-by-step emergency protocols. Therefore, with a flight surgeon up to 22 minutes away each way on Mars, crews must spot problems early and act on their own. Our protocols and escalation advice change with the comms delay, and one short report to Mission Control replaces a slow back-and-forth. Tested on real NASA Inspiration4 blood data, our method flagged 4 changes that normal ranges missed. It is important as catching silent changes early and fast could protect crew health on deep-space missions and in other remote places.
details: Crew Health Monitor is a health companion for astronauts on long missions, where a flight surgeon can be up to 22 minutes away each way. It compares every reading with Earth ranges and with the astronaut’s own recent normal, and shows the worse of the two. Rules link signals into plain-language early warnings, such as short sleep plus stress pointing to a possible infection. Astronauts also get space-specific self-checks, a hydration log and emergency protocols that change with the comms delay. Medical officers get a body map, trends and a short report for ground.Crews can catch silent changes early and act without waiting for ground. Mood data stays private unless the astronaut shares it. Tested on real NASA Inspiration4 blood data, our method flagged 4 changes that normal ranges missed. The same idea could help submarines, Antarctic stations and remote clinics. Vite and plain JavaScript for the web app. Python (pandas, numpy) to process NASA data and generate a synthetic 90-day mission. An optional AI helper phrases emergency guidance. All triage runs as fixed rules. We used Claude to help write code and text.Personal baselines, linked signals and delay-aware advice. We considered comms delay, privacy and false alarms, and we label what is synthetic and what is a demo threshold.
